mainTopic: The פרת as a source of water and its use for immersion; the משנה exempting bought or gifted animals from מעשר בהמה
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a discussion about whether the פרת (Euphrates) is the source of other waters. The גמרא challenges this from springs that sit higher than the river, and רב משרשיא answers that the water climbs up underground like 'ladders.' A second challenge comes from a פסוק that calls the פרת the 'fourth river,' and רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that it is really the original river that came out of עדן. A ברייתא from רבי מאיר adds that the river's first name is יובל, and that it is called פרת because its waters multiply. This supports שמואל, who says a river grows from its own bed, and it goes against רב, who says the פרת rises from rain in ארץ ישראל. The גמרא then tells how שמואל's father made a מקוה for his daughters in ניסן, because the river might be mostly rainwater, but let them use the river itself in תשרי. The גמרא notes that one of שמואל's rulings seems to contradict his own view. A new משנה then teaches that bought or gifted animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה. רב כהנא begins to give the source from a פסוק about firstborn sons and animals, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from springs that are higher than the Euphrates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the פרת feeds other waters, because some springs are higher up than the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are springs that are higher up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the claim, made on the previous amud, that all waters come from the פרת. It points to springs located higher than the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water flows downhill. A spring up in the mountains sits above the פרת, so it seems impossible for the river's water to reach it. That seems to disprove the idea that the פרת is the source.
steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of an argument. The claim being challenged, that the פרת feeds other waters, was stated on the previous amud.

phrases.english: But there are springs that are higher up!
phrases.notes: This is a challenge: water can't flow uphill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim (on the previous amud) that the פרת is the source of other waters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פרת feeds other rivers and springs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Water flows downward. Springs higher than the פרת cannot be fed by it.

steps.title: The higher springs are fed by 'ladders' of the Euphrates
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that the river's water climbs up underground and comes out at those higher springs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: Those springs are the 'ladders' of the פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers the challenge. The פרת's water travels underground and rises up, as if climbing a ladder, until it comes out at the higher springs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed water can only move downhill. רב משרשיא says that underground the water is drawn upward. So a spring can sit higher than the river and still come from it, and the original claim stands.

keyTerms.meaning: ladders (here: underground channels that carry water upward)

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
Those are ladders of the Euphrates.
phrases.notes: The river's water seeps through the ground and rises up to come out at those springs.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining how the claim works in practice (water rising underground)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Springs higher than the פרת cannot come from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרת's water climbs underground and comes out at the higher springs, so they still come from the פרת.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse calling the Euphrates the 'fourth river'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again from a פסוק that lists the פרת last among the four rivers of עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And the fourth river is the פרת'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a פסוק in בראשית. The פסוק calls the פרת the fourth river, which makes it sound like the last and least of the rivers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית, one river comes out of עדן and splits into four heads. The פרת is listed fourth. If it is just one of the branches, and the last one listed, how can it be the main source of other waters?

keyTerms.meaning: but it is written (opens a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And the fourth river is the Euphrates"!
phrases.notes: בראשית ב:יד. The פרת is listed last of the four branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first challenge was answered. Now a new challenge comes from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פרת is the source of other waters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists the פרת as the fourth branch, which suggests it is a minor branch and not the source.

steps.title: The Euphrates is the original river that came out of עדן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק (or רב אחא בר יעקב) explains that the פרת is the river mentioned at the very beginning, the one that came out of עדן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said, and some say it was רב אחא בר יעקב: It is the פרת that was mentioned at the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer re-reads the פסוק. The words 'it is the פרת' point back to the original river that flowed out of עדן, not just to the fourth branch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original river split off three branches, and what continued flowing was still the פרת. So the פרת is both listed fourth and the original source. Being listed last does not make it the least important. It is the main river that the others branched out from.

keyTerms.meaning: from the beginning / the original one

steps.confusionAlert: The פרת is not being taken off the list of four rivers. The point is that the river listed fourth is the same original river from עדן, which kept flowing after the other three split off.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the claim that the פרת is the source of other waters. That claim matters for the earlier discussion it came from.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said,
and some say it was Rav Acha bar Yaakov:
It is the Euphrates of the beginning.
phrases.notes: It is the same river that first came out of עדן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרת is only the fourth and least of the branches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'it is the פרת' refer back to the original river from עדן, which continued as the פרת after the others split off.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the river's name is יובל, and why it is called פרת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי מאיר says the river's name is יובל, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו, and that it is called פרת because its waters multiply.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says its name is יובל, as it says, 'He shall be like a tree planted by water, that sends out its roots by the יובל.' So why is it called פרת? Because its waters are fruitful and multiply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more information about this great river. רבי מאיר gives its original name, יובל, and explains the meaning of the name פרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name פרת comes from פרים ורבים, 'fruitful and multiplying.' Its waters keep growing even without rain. This fits the idea that the פרת is a powerful source that can feed other waters.

keyTerms.meaning: Yuval, a stream (רבי מאיר says this is the river's name)

steps.whatToRemember: The פרת is presented as the master river. Its water can rise underground to feed higher springs. It is the original river that came out of עדן. Its name means its waters multiply by themselves.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita, Rabbi Meir says:
"Yuval" is its name,
as it is stated: "For he shall be like a tree planted by the waters
and that sends out its roots by the river (yuval)",
And why is it called "Perat"?
Because its waters are fruitful and multiply.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: פרת comes from פרים. The waters grow even without rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about the river's names that fits the picture of the פרת as a great, self-multiplying river.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The river's original name is יובל. It is called פרת because its waters are fruitful and multiply.

steps.title: The name פרת supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's explanation of the name פרת supports שמואל's view that a river's water grows from its own bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports שמואל, who said: a river is blessed from its own bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא we just learned backs up a statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the river is called פרת because its waters multiply. שמואל says a river's extra water comes up from its own bed, not from rain. A river that "multiplies" by itself fits שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: From its own bed (its banks or source)

phrases.english: This supports Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:
A river is blessed (increases) from its own bed.
phrases.notes: The extra water comes from underground sources, not from rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a supporting inference from the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that a river's water grows from its own bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that the פרת is named for its waters multiplying.

steps.title: This disagrees with רב, who says the פרת rises from rain
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא disagrees with רב, who says the rise of the פרת is evidence of rain in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it disagrees with רב, for רב אמי said in the name of רב: when rain falls in the West (ארץ ישראל), the great witness to it is the פרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that the ברייתא goes against רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that the פרת swells because of rain far away in ארץ ישראל. So in his view the river's extra water is rainwater, not water from its own bed. This is the opposite of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rav,
for Rav Ami said in the name of Rav:
Rain in the West (Eretz Yisrael):
its great witness is the Euphrates.
phrases.notes: When the Euphrates rises, you know it rained in ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flip side of step 6: the ברייתא supports שמואל and goes against רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the פרת swells from rain in ארץ ישראל, so its added water is rainwater.

steps.title: The practice of שמואל's father for his daughters
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל made a מקוה for his daughters in ניסן and set out mats at the river in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father made a מקוה for his daughters in the days of ניסן, and set out mats in the days of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how שמואל's father arranged immersion for his daughters. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains why he did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ניסן he did not let them use the river. He built them a separate מקוה. In תשרי they immersed in the river itself, and he set out mats in the water. Rashi explains: Tishrei riverbanks hold soft mud, and the cane mats under their feet kept the mud from rising onto their feet and interposing (חציצה) during the immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: A gathered pool of water for immersion
Spring month (after the rainy season) / autumn month (after the dry summer)

phrases.english: Shmuel's father made for his daughters
a mikveh in the days of Nisan,
and mats in the days of Tishrei.
phrases.notes: In Tishrei they immersed in the river. Rabbeinu Tam explains the mats gave them privacy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life practice connected to the רב vs. שמואל question about the river's water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ניסן: a separate מקוה. In תשרי: immersion in the river itself.

steps.title: Why a מקוה in ניסן: he held like רב
steps.stepSummary: The ניסן מקוה is explained: he followed רב, and worried that rainwater would be the majority of the flowing river.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מקוה in ניסן: he held like רב, for רב אמי said in the name of רב: when rain falls in the West, the great witness is the פרת. He worried that the rainwater might outnumber the flowing spring water, so the rainwater would be the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the story: why he built a מקוה in ניסן instead of using the river.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spring water purifies even while it flows, but rainwater purifies only when gathered and still in a מקוה. After the rainy season, רב says the פרת is full of rain. So the river might be mostly rainwater, and flowing rainwater cannot purify.

keyTerms.meaning: Flowing waters, meaning spring or river water

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think all water purifies the same way. Water from a spring (מעיין) purifies even while flowing. Rainwater purifies only when gathered and standing in a מקוה. That is the whole reason a river full of rain is a problem.

phrases.english: A mikveh in the days of Nisan:
he held like Rav,
for Rav Ami said in the name of Rav:
rain in the West, its great witness is the Euphrates;
perhaps the dripping (rain) waters will outnumber the flowing (spring) waters,
and the rainwater will be the majority.
phrases.notes: Flowing rainwater does not purify, so he needed a still מקוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְוֶה בְּיוֹמֵי נִיסָן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the story in step 8 using רב's view from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the rainy season the פרת may be mostly rainwater, and flowing rainwater does not purify, so a still מקוה is needed.

steps.title: Why only mats in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the second half of the story: in תשרי the river was used directly, with only mats set out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And mats in the days of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the words about תשרי to explain the second half of the story. The text does not state the reason outright, but it follows from the previous step, as explained below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the dry summer there has been no rain, so the river in תשרי is all its own spring-like water. That water purifies even while flowing, so the daughters could immerse right in the river. Rashi explains the mats: standing on them kept the soft riverbed mud off their feet, so nothing would interpose (חוצץ) between them and the water.

phrases.english: And mats in the days of Tishrei.
phrases.notes: No rain in summer, so in Tishrei the river is not rain-fed and may be used while flowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation begun in step 9, now for the תשרי half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In תשרי the river is not rain-fed, so flowing river water may be used for immersion.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that שמואל's statement that a river grows from its own bed conflicts with his other ruling that flowing water purifies only in the פרת during תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his own statement disagrees with his other statement, for שמואל said: waters do not purify while flowing, except the פרת in the days of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two statements of שמואל don't fit together. No answer is given here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a river grows only from its own bed (step 6), the פרת should purify while flowing all year. Yet שמואל limits it to תשרי. That limit implies that at other times the river is mostly rainwater, which is רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: His own statement disagrees with his own other statement
Purify, meaning they are valid for immersion

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the פרת rises from rain, and שמואל (in one statement) says it rises from its own bed. Flowing water purifies only if it is not mostly rainwater. That is why אבוה דשמואל and שמואל's own ruling allow the river only in תשרי, after the dry summer.

phrases.english: And his own statement disagrees with his own other statement,
for Shmuel said:
Waters do not purify while flowing
except the Euphrates in the days of Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's statement in step 6 and sets it against his own ruling, which matches the תשרי practice in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that a river grows from its own bed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling that flowing water purifies only in the פרת during תשרי assumes the river is rain-fed at other times, which contradicts his claim that it grows from its own bed.

steps.title: Bought or gifted animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that animals a person buys, or receives as a gift, are exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who buys an animal, or who was given an animal as a gift, is exempt from מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It teaches that the obligation of מעשר בהמה does not apply to animals you bought or were given as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה means that every tenth animal of the herd is made holy. This משנה limits that obligation to animals that came into your possession in the normal way, by being born in your herd. An animal that came to you by purchase or as a gift stays outside the count.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe: every tenth animal of the herd is made holy

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the topic for the coming סוגיא. The גמרא will now look for the פסוק that teaches this exemption.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: One who buys an animal, or to whom it was given as a gift
is exempt from animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ, אוֹ שֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Unrelated to the river discussion. This opens a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals acquired by purchase or as a gift are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: What is the source for this exemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the משנה. The גמרא wants to find the פסוק that teaches why a bought or gifted animal is exempt from מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? (asks for the source)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that bought or gifted animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: רב כהנא begins with the verse about firstborn sons and animals
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא quotes a פסוק that puts the firstborn of your sons next to your cattle and sheep. The rest of the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא says: The פסוק states, "The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me. So you shall do with your oxen and with your sheep."
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא begins to answer by quoting a פסוק. The פסוק links the law of your firstborn sons to your animals, and the גמרא is about to explain how this teaches the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "so you shall do" compare your animals to your sons. A son is yours only by birth, not by purchase or gift. רב כהנא will use this comparison to show that a law about animals applies only to animals born into your possession. How this law about the בכור carries over to מעשר בהמה continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: So shall you do (makes a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק is about the בכור (firstborn), not about מעשר בהמה. Do not get stuck on that. The גמרא will explain the link between them in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana says:
As the verse states:
"The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me;
so you shall do with your oxen and with your sheep,"
phrases.notes: שמות כב:כח–כט. What the גמרא learns from this פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק that compares your animals to your firstborn sons ("so shall you do with your oxen and sheep"). The full derivation continues on the next amud.
